info.title: The Stacks API v1
info.description: A single, continuously-evolving REST surface: additive changes (new fields, new optional params, new endpoints) ship without a version bump; breaking changes are a v2 conversation. See `/api/v0` for the frozen, pre-versioning API.

AutoImportFormat.description: Pick the format from the source.

DraftImportTarget.description: Re-import into this publication's draft: its title, subtitle, abstract and body are replaced and the document becomes its current import. Contributors, orgs, tags, license and linked assets are kept. The caller must be able to edit the publication.

singleLineBreaks.description: How a single line break (Shift+Enter) is imported: as a new paragraph (the default) or as a line break within the paragraph. Two or more in a row always start a new paragraph.

GoogleDocsImportFormat.description: A Google Doc, converted to MyST markdown.

settled.description: False while media is still being copied to Raven. Until then the draft body holds `raven-media://` refs and can't be edited or published.

validationErrors.description: Problems that didn't stop the import, e.g. contributors that couldn't be matched to a Raven user and were skipped, and anything the draft still needs before it can be published.

UrlImportSource.description: A publicly shared document. Only Google Docs URLs are supported so far.

slug.description: Slug for the access URL for the publication, e.g. https://thestacks.org/publications/{slug}. If another publication already uses the slug, the first free variant (`{slug}-2`, `{slug}-3`, ...) is stored instead and reported in `validationErrors` with code `slug_replaced`.

subjects.description: The DataCite subjects for the publication's DOIs, as a full list that replaces the stored one; the rest of its DOI metadata is left untouched. Needs at least one subject, each non-empty. Rejected once the publication is published. DataCite receives them the next time one of the publication's DOIs is minted or updated.

get.description: Viewable by a contributor, a site admin, or (once the publication has at least one org attached) any member of one of those orgs — broader than the edit permission `PATCH .../id/{id}/draft` requires. With `Accept: text/markdown; variant=myst`, the draft comes back as a MyST document built from its current fields (`title`, `subtitle`, `abstract`, `license` as an SPDX ID, `keywords` from the tags, `doi`, then the body), which `PUT .../id/{id}/draft/content` accepts back unchanged. JSON stays the default; plain `text/markdown` isn't offered. With `Accept: application/vnd.thestacks.mdast+json; schema=1; version=3`, a MyST version comes back as its MyST AST, for rendering. `schema` and `version` are optional (default: the latest) and must come before any `q`; an older `version` is migrated down, a newer one gets the latest. The AST is only sent when its type is named explicitly and preferred over the other types offered. Its `ETag` is for `If-None-Match`, not `If-Match`. The draft's AST carries `messages` and is private.

get.summary: Get a publication version by slug
get.description: Returns the given version of a publication, identified by slug, if the caller has access to it (published versions are public; draft versions require view/edit permission). A deleted publication that once had a DOI-bearing version always returns that last published version instead, regardless of the version requested, so the DOI keeps resolving. Responds with JSON by default; append `.md` or `.json` to `versionNumber` (e.g. `v3.md`) or send `Accept: text/markdown` for a clean Markdown rendering intended for AI agents/crawlers. An explicit suffix always wins over the `Accept` header. With `Accept: application/vnd.thestacks.mdast+json; schema=1; version=3`, a MyST version comes back as its MyST AST, for rendering. `schema` and `version` are optional (default: the latest) and must come before any `q`; an older `version` is migrated down, a newer one gets the latest. The AST is only sent when its type is named explicitly and preferred over the other types offered. Its `ETag` is for `If-None-Match`, not `If-Match`. A draft version's AST carries `messages` and is private.

get.description: Without `q`: a paginated list of all active users, newest first. With `q`: up to 20 users ranked by relevance to the query (username, ORCID, or name); `page`/`perPage` are ignored in this mode. A signed-in caller may also search by email or the start of one; for anyone else, an email query matches no one. Combines v0's `GET /users/` and `GET /users/search`.

200.description: Users matching `q`, or the full paginated list.

422.description: The request's path parameters, query, headers, cookies, or body failed validation.

post.description: Converts the document at `source` and creates a draft publication from the result, owned by the caller. `format` defaults to `auto`, which picks the format from the source. Only Google Docs URLs are supported so far. With `target: { type: "draft", publicationId }` the document is re-imported into that publication's draft instead (see `DraftImportTarget`). Media in the document is copied to Raven in the background; follow its progress with `GET /imports/{importId}`.

201.description: The draft publication was created, or the target draft was re-imported.

400.description: The source isn't a supported document.

403.description: The caller can't create publications (or edit the target publication), or the source document isn't accessible to Raven (e.g. a private document).

404.description: The source document doesn't exist, or the target publication or its draft doesn't (including a draft published or deleted while the document was being converted).

409.description: The target draft's media from an earlier import is still being copied to Raven. Retry once `GET /imports/{importId}` for that import reports `settled`.

422.description: The request's path parameters, query, headers, cookies, or body failed validation.

502.description: The source couldn't be fetched or read, e.g. its server returned an error or rate-limited Raven. Retrying later may work.
